# agy 1.2.13 stream-json captures

`denial-replay.stdout.ndjson` replays two turns from one real 1.2.13 process: a denied shell
command, then a text-only answer whose result retains the first denial. The replay clock is
synthetic; frames retain the native cumulative denial payload.

Captured on Linux x86_64 on 2026-09-29. These are observations from the supplied binary, not guarantees for the Google sign-in route. No product code or capture drivers are included.

Each row names a capture prefix. Its `.stdin.ndjson`, `.stdout.ndjson`, `.stderr.ndjson`, and `.capture.ndjson` companions keep the streams separate; empty streams are empty files. Every line wraps the exact decoded JSON frame or text line in `{t_ms, stream, data}`. `t_ms` is milliseconds since construction immediately before spawn. Capture annotations record launch arguments, configuration, signals, EOF, timeouts, and exit code; they are not CLI output. Line references refer to the indicated file, starting at 1.

Commands below run from `<WORKSPACE>`. `<AGY>` expands to `<HOME>/.local/opt/agy/1.2.13/agy` in the real installation home; the child uses a separate isolated `<HOME>` for state. All captures remove inherited credential/provider environment variables, set `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<HOME>/.config`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME=<HOME>/.cache`, `XDG_DATA_HOME=<HOME>/.local/share`, `BROWSER=/bin/true`, and loopback-only `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy`. Neither PATH nor shell rc files changed. Resume rows reuse the original isolated HOME.

For rows marked **API**, the environment also contains `GEMINI_API_KEY=<DUMMY_KEY>` and `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>`, and `<HOME>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` contains `{"modelProvider":"gemini"}`. **Env only** sets those two variables without the setting; **None** has neither. The loopback translator reused the prior QA route and forwarded real requests to a paid upstream model. Its credential was read programmatically inside the temporary proxy, with later captures passing it through the proxy environment. It was never passed to agy or recorded. The translator maps all requested Gemini models to one upstream Gemini model: request routing and CLI selection are verified, native model identity/quality is not.

The translator emits text, function calls, thought parts and usage. Its usage mapping does not populate Gemini thinking/cache counts, so observed zero `thinking_tokens`/`cache_read_tokens` does not prove native zeros. No dedicated reasoning frames appeared, including the matched high-effort probe.

`<HOME>`, `<WORKSPACE>`, `<CAPTURE>`, `<PORT>`, `<DUMMY_KEY>`, and `<REDACTED_REFERENCE>` are redactions. Unrelated project/model names and help examples are redacted without removing frames. Delta chunk boundaries remain; a path split across deltas can have a different placeholder spelling than the complete result. UUIDs are retained for conversation correlation.

`project-skill` used `<WORKSPACE>/.agents/skills/phase0-marker/SKILL.md` with name `phase0-marker`, description “Return the Phase 0 marker when requested,” and instructions “Respond with PHASE0_SKILL_MARKER. No tools are needed after reading this skill.”

Each tools capture begins with `input.txt` containing `PHASE0_READ_MARKER`, then requests create→replace from `PHASE0_WRITE` to `PHASE0_EDIT`, then `printf PHASE0_SHELL`. `state-inspection.ndjson` records the resulting files. These successful writes disprove an enforced read-only boundary for default/plan on this credential route. `--sandbox` alone still denies the shell at permission policy, so OS sandbox enforcement is unverified.

## MCP discovery

Phase 0 project setup (`mcp-project` and `mcp-project-isolated`) places `{"mcpServers":{"phase0":{"serverUrl":"http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/mcp"}}}` in `<WORKSPACE>/.agents/mcp_config.json`. `mcp-project-config` instead uses `<WORKSPACE>/.gemini/config.json`; that file did not expose the server. HTTP calls send string arguments and fail strict validation.

Phase 2 places the same HTTP configuration, named `phase2`, in a plugin-owned `<CAPTURE>/owned/.agents/mcp_config.json`. Both add-dir orders discover it, as does launching in the owned directory and adding the real workspace. All three turns execute shell `pwd` in the owned directory. The file turns read the workspace marker but also write `output.txt` into the owned directory. These routes fail the requirement that tools resolve against the user's workspace. Reordering arguments did not change the observed shell cwd; the precise directory selection rule is unverified.

The external `--agent` file, nested agent definition, and flat definition with an `agents.json` manifest contain inline `mcpServers`. Native logs record “not found, falling back to default” for each. These experiments do not establish that every agent definition format is unsupported. `parity-inspection.ndjson` records their definitions and log evidence. Searching the tested binary's strings found no `AGY_MCP`, `MCP_CONFIG`, `AGY_CONFIG`, or `ANTIGRAVITY_CONFIG` override; no environment discovery route was verified.

No tested MCP route satisfies both discovery and workspace ownership. MCP implementation stopped at this gate: no relay or MCP capability change was added. Images and the daemon e2e continued independently. No global MCP configuration exists in the isolated homes, and no configuration was written into the user repository.

## Image file fallback

`image-file-external.png` contains a red triangle on the left and a blue circle on the lower right, against white. The prompt supplies only its path and asks for visible shapes and colors. `image-file-external.stdout.ndjson:4–5` records a successful `view_file`; the result describes the pixels correctly. The native function response supplies bytes at `functionResponse.parts[].inlineData`. The temporary translator was corrected to forward these nested parts to the model; forwarding top-level parts alone dropped the image. `parity-inspection.ndjson` records the image hash and response-part location.

This verifies one default-mode CLI turn reading a file outside the workspace without an extra add-dir. A later isolated-daemon run attached the same image through the provider and returned the same shapes and colors after a successful `view_file`. The provider advertises `prompt.image`; MCP remains outside the parity implementation.

Unverified: Google login behaviour; native reasoning/cached-token accounting; filesystem/network isolation under sandbox plus approved commands; exhaustive tool policy; other agent definition formats or environment MCP overrides; child transcript streaming beyond parent metadata; a stable public conversation-list command. No fresh login was created. The fetched official manifest returned 1.2.12 while this binary reports 1.2.13; the checksum identifies the tested binary, but that response does not establish its release provenance.
